subject: body
title: Muscles
about: How muscles move you: they pull on bones through tendons, work in pairs so an arm can bend and straighten, and come in two kinds, the ones you steer (arms, legs, jaw, tongue, smile) and the ones that run on their own (heart, stomach); also how many you have (about 600), what they need (protein, rest, stretching), why you shiver and which muscle is the biggest. Inside-the-body anatomy is a bridge topic beyond NC Grade 1; the nearest codes are PE.1.HF.3.1 and PE.1.HF.3.2 (muscle strength and the benefits of activity) and 1.NPA.1.2 and 1.NPA.2.1 (foods and activity that build a strong body). Read it together: the tablet reads every card aloud while he bends his arm, makes a muscle and feels his jaw.
tip: Have him bend his arm and feel the biceps bunch up, then straighten it and feel the back of his arm tighten instead.

cards.q: Muscles move your bones. Do they push the bones or pull them?
cards.note: A muscle can only pull. It gets shorter and tugs on the bone it is tied to.

cards.q: What tough cord ties a muscle to a bone?
cards.note: Feel the tight cord above your heel. That is the Achilles tendon, the biggest one you have.

cards.q: Bend your arm. The front muscle pulls. What does its partner on the back of your arm do?
cards.note: Muscles work in pairs. To straighten your arm, the back muscle pulls and the front one relaxes.

cards.q: Make a muscle! The bump on the front of your upper arm is called your...?
cards.note: Say BY-seps. It bends your elbow, and the triceps on the back of your arm straightens it again.

cards.q: About how many muscles do you have?
cards.note: More than 600 muscles, big and small. Your face alone has more than 40.

cards.q: Which muscle squeezes all day and all night and never takes a rest?
cards.note: The heart is a muscle that squeezes more than once every second, even while you sleep.

cards.q: Which muscle works on its own, without you telling it to?
cards.note: Stomach and heart muscles run on their own, even in your sleep. Arm and leg muscles wait for your orders.

cards.q: You smile at a friend. What is pulling the corners of your mouth up?
cards.note: Little muscles in your cheeks lift your smile. A frown uses a different set.

cards.q: Stick out your tongue and wiggle it. What is your tongue made of?
cards.note: The tongue is a bundle of muscles with no bone inside. It pushes food to your teeth and shapes your words.

cards.q: Eggs, beans, fish and meat have a muscle-building part in them. What is it called?
cards.note: Say PRO-teen. Muscles use protein as building blocks to mend and grow, and milk, nuts and yogurt have it too.

cards.q: The day after a big hike, your legs feel a little sore. What does that soreness mean?
cards.note: Hard work makes tiny changes in muscles. Rest and sleep mend them, and they come back stronger.

cards.q: Why do you stretch before you run and play?
cards.note: Stretching warms muscles up so they bend easily and do not get hurt.

cards.q: You are cold and you start to shiver. What is shivering?
cards.note: Working muscles make heat, so shivering warms you up. Put on a coat and they can stop.

cards.q: The biggest muscle in your body is the one you...?
cards.note: The big muscle in your bottom helps you stand up, climb stairs and jump.

cards.q: Chew a crunchy carrot and touch your cheeks. Which muscles are squeezing?
cards.note: Jaw muscles are some of the strongest for their size. They bite through apples and carrots.

cards.q: You stand still in line. Are your muscles resting or working?
cards.note: Lots of small muscles hold you up even when you stand still. Lie down and they finally get a rest.
